_about: THE classification table for everything a restore can write. Default-deny: a path or key that is not listed here is EXCLUDED and the dry run says 'not restored: unknown item <name>'. Each row has exactly one class. excluded = never restored (with the reason and what to redo). data = a value that no code path turns into behaviour: typed, carrying no words, read by nothing but the program's own arithmetic or lookups, and saying which code reads it (comes back without a tick). runs = anything else that is read: by a model (a prompt, a tool result, a memory, a note, a name it says), spoken or sent to someone, choosing a network destination, changing trust, consent, routing, numbers or timing of call handling, re-sent by a button, or acting when a person presses an ordinary button (listed by name and value, unticked by default, applied only when its tick is ticked). Order matters: the first row that matches wins. The docs section of docs/BACKUP.md is generated from this file (a test fails when they differ), and tests walk the real writers and fail when a store is not classified here.

All of that needs the tick. Only the opening hours and the steps between the times offered are typed values that carry no words and come back without one. The sync with FormLogic is never restored.

desktop.what: The messages callers left for you
desktop.reason: Each holds what a caller said and the number they rang from or asked to be rung on. A file that was not made by you could put words in front of you, and numbers to ring back, that no caller left; and a restore replaces the messages that are here, which are your record of what callers asked and of what you did about it.

desktop.what: Transfer settings, key by key (see the transfer table)
desktop.reason: They are the owner's policy for putting callers through: whether the receptionist may try to reach you at all (it is off until you turn it on), whom and when, which numbers ring whatever the limits and the quiet hours say, and how often. Every key needs the transfers tick, so a backup that was not ticked for it cannot turn transfers on, name a number that rings whatever the limits say, or silence your phones. Which devices ring, and a timed 'away', are never restored.

desktop.what: The tries to put callers through in the last hour
desktop.reason: The callers' numbers and the moments of the last hour's tries: it is what enforces the hourly limits. A restored one would count tries that were made on another computer, or at another time, against callers here; it starts again.
desktop.reads: Only the limits read it, to count a caller's tries in the last hour; it feeds no other behaviour. It is excluded because it is run state of the computer that made it, and it holds callers' numbers.

desktop.what: Who may use this computer: the access model's credentials, sessions, owner record, audit trail and throttle, and the web login's password record, sessions, setup code and console
desktop.reason: It decides who can reach OAIY and what they may do: the paired programs and apps and what each holds, the owner's password record, the sessions and the failed attempts that are being held back. A backup never holds it and a restore never replaces it: a file that was not made here must not be able to add a credential, remove the owner or clear a block. The audit trail is the record of what was done with them. Nothing of it is brought back.
desktop.redo: Sign in, and pair your programs and apps, again on this computer.
desktop.reads: The guard of every route reads the credentials, the owner record and the throttle to decide who may call it; the audit trail is written by the guard and shown to the owner, and nothing reads it as an instruction. All of it is excluded because it is who may reach this computer, not a setting of it.

calendar.about: The calendar: the business's settings and its appointments. The words in it (the business's and the receptionist's names, each service's name, price and description, and each appointment's service, name, phone number and notes) are read by the receptionist and the Agent and said to callers, so they need the calendar tick. audit.reads: The page's themes ship inside the program (the folder theme is looked in, not written); a person's choice of theme lives in the browser and is not in the data folder or in the Agent's storage that a backup reads. It feeds no behaviour.
audit.why: Nothing is stored that a restore could write, so there is nothing to classify.

audit.reads: There is none of its own: a text conversation is a conversation of the front desk (opfs/front-desk/sessions), and the texts' settings are the Agent's settings (messages.*). Both are rows of this table. The messages callers leave for the owner are a store of the desktop of their own (messages/messages.json: the row `messages`, with its own tick).
audit.why: A store that appears later is refused by the scanner tests until it is classified.

scan._about: Every name the desktop's own code uses for a file or a folder under its data folder, and every name the Agent's page uses in its browser storage, mapped to the row that classifies it or to the reason it is not a store. A test reads the sources and fails when a name is not here, so a new store cannot be added without a decision.

agentModules.desktop/backup.ts: The Agent's half of the backup: it reads its storage to export it, and writes only what the desktop lists when a restore is applied.
agentModules.main.ts: Only asks the browser to keep its storage (navigator.storage.persist): it writes nothing.
agentModules.settings.ts: IndexedDB (database bot.computer, store kv): the Agent's settings.
agentModules.vfs/projects.ts: The private file system: the projects and the front desk.
agentModules.vfs/transfer.ts: Exports a project to a folder the person picks on their own disk (the File System Access API): it does not touch the Agent's storage.
